findings.description: The purpose-claim hardening is applied to only one of the two session entry points in the file the diff touched. get_current_user now goes through session_user_id (rejects any JWT carrying a `purpose` claim), but get_current_admin still calls decode_access_token directly and accepts any token that has an `admin_sub` claim, with no purpose check. No exploit exists today (nothing in app/ mints a token containing `admin_sub`, and pending_2fa tokens carry `sub`, not `admin_sub`), so this is not a reachable bypass, but the invariant 'a purpose-bound token is never a session' is only half enforced and will silently regress the moment an admin purpose-bound token (e.g. admin pending-2FA) is introduced.
findings.fix: In get_current_admin, reject purpose-bound tokens too: after `payload = decode_access_token(access_token)`, add `if "purpose" in payload: raise HTTPException(401, ...)` (or extract a shared `_session_claims(token)` helper in auth_service used by both dependencies).

findings.description: The diff rewrote this import line to add session_user_id but left decode_access_token imported; after the change it has no use anywhere in the module (the only decode path is session_user_id at line 27). ruff F401 would flag it, and the context pack records that ruff/mypy were not runnable in this venv, so the lint gate did not catch it.
findings.fix: Change line 12 to `from app.services.auth_service import session_user_id`. (`json` at line 2 and `get_db` at line 9 are also unused but were already unused before this change - leave them or clean separately.)

findings.description: CHG-004 AC2 and the risk-map entry say the socket is 'closed with code 1008'. Closing before accept() is the correct and secure choice, but per the ASGI spec a `websocket.close` sent in the CONNECTING state makes the server (uvicorn) reject the handshake with an HTTP 403 response; the 1008 close code is never put on the wire. The assertion in tests/unit/test_notifications.py:87-94 holds only because Starlette's TestClient surfaces the ASGI close message as WebSocketDisconnect(1008). Denial behaviour is correct either way; only the client-visible signal differs from the wording of the AC.
findings.fix: No code change needed. Note in CHG-004/risk-map R18 that real clients see an HTTP 403 handshake rejection (the 1008 code is the ASGI-level signal), so a future frontend does not wait for a close frame that never arrives.

findings.description: The pending_2fa token is not single-use. delete_cookie clears the browser's copy, but the JWT itself stays valid for the remainder of its 10 minutes, and verify_totp_code does not check user.totp_verified. A captured pending token plus a valid TOTP code could therefore mint a second 8-hour session after enrolment completed. Exposure is small (HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Lax cookie, <=10 min, still needs a live TOTP code) and AC4 only requires clearing the cookie, so this is a follow-up, not a defect against the story.
findings.fix: Cheapest hardening: after the user lookup, `if user.totp_verified: raise HTTPException(400, 'TOTP already verified.')` - a replayed pending token then cannot re-open a session. A jti denylist would be the fuller fix.

findings.description: AC2 has two halves: a user_id query parameter is ignored, and the user comes from the cookie. Only the no-cookie half is tested (test_verify_without_pending_cookie_is_401_even_with_a_user_id). No test sends a valid pending token for user A together with `?user_id=B` and asserts the lookup still uses A. The suite is otherwise strong (69 passed; the reject-parametrisations assert db.queries == 0 / commits == 0, and the WS tests assert not-accepted and an empty registry, so they genuinely bite).
findings.fix: Add one case to test_verify_with_pending_token_and_good_code_opens_a_session using `params={"user_id": "someone-else"}` and keep the existing `users.id = 'user-123'` SQL assertion.
